paper_metadata.title: Quantum Quantitative Trading: High-Frequency Statistical Arbitrage Algorithm

summary: This paper proposes a gate-based quantum statistical arbitrage pipeline for high-frequency trading, combining variable-time condition-number preselection with quantum cointegration testing. The main claimed complexities are O(sqrt(d) kappa_0^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) for preselection and O(d^2.5 kappa^3 / delta^2 poly(log^2(d kappa / delta)) + dN + (L+2)^2.5 kappa'^3 / delta'^2 poly(log^2((L+2)kappa'/delta'))) for the cointegration test, with a rough estimate of more than 50 qubits and no experimental hardware results.

experiments.description: Quantum statistical arbitrage pipeline for fixed condition-number preselection followed by quantum cointegration testing on portfolios of stock price time series.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Statistical Arbitrage Algorithm with Fixed Condition Number Preselection + Quantum Cointegration Test

hyperparameters.d: number of stocks in one portfolio

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Historical stock prices are loaded into qRAM via |j⟩|t⟩|z⟩ -> |j⟩|t⟩|z ⊕ p_t^(j)⟩; portfolios are represented as amplitude-encoded or register-encoded time-series data. The preselection step uses a Hermitian embedding A = [[0, X],[X^T, 0]] for condition-number estimation; the cointegration test uses quantum linear regression on the design matrix X and then a second regression on lagged residuals.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Select multicollinear portfolios with condition number κ >= κ0, then test whether the portfolio residuals are stationary via Engle-Granger two-step cointegration test (ADF on residuals).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold-based filtering on condition number; portfolios failing preselection are skipped. Cointegration is accepted if the ADF test statistic exceeds the critical-value criterion for stationarity rejection/acceptance as described.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Hermitian embedding A = [[0, X],[X^T, 0]] used for linear-system/phase-estimation style routines.

problem_instance.description: High-frequency statistical arbitrage on U.S. stock market time series; portfolios are formed from many stocks and tested for multicollinearity and cointegration.

dataset_specification.description: Half-second aggregated quotes; about 253 trading days/year; no explicit ticker list or date range given.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical prices are loaded into qRAM; the paper discusses using stock price matrices and residual construction from linear regression, but does not specify additional preprocessing beyond the statistical-arbitrage setup.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides theoretical complexity analysis and a realistic-case estimate; no empirical benchmark runs or repeated trials are reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical matrix multiplication, vector subtraction, and classical computation of the ADF test statistic / critical-value comparison are used as hybrid postprocessing.
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load price data into qRAM; form portfolio matrices; construct Hermitian embedding; prepare amplitude-encoded data for QLR/QCNC routines.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute predicted values Xβ, residuals y - Xβ, lagged residuals, standard error, Dickey-Fuller test statistic, and compare against critical values.

results.value: O(d^2.5 kappa^3 / delta^2 poly(log^2(d kappa / delta)) + dN + (L+2)^2.5 kappa'^3 / delta'^2 poly(log^2((L+2)kappa'/delta')))

results.unit: time points per stock per year

speedup_claims.conditions: U.S. stock market example with N ≈ 1.2 x 10^7, about 8000 stocks, and kappa_0 = 1000
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a back-of-the-envelope scalability estimate, not a measured speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(d) kappa_0^2 log(1/epsilon)^2) for preselection; O(d^2.5 kappa^3 / delta^2 poly(log^2(d kappa / delta)) + dN + (L+2)^2.5 kappa'^3 / delta'^2 poly(log^2((L+2)kappa'/delta')) ) for cointegration test
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N^2 d) benchmark for the overall statistical-arbitrage task; O(N^3) for classical preselection via matrix factorization is also cited

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: qRAM access, roughly >50 logical qubits for the full pipeline estimate, and efficient implementation of phase-estimation/linear-systems subroutines
